analysis: Reject D1 as a blocking defect. Its causal observation is correct: base interpolates null and 42 through string coercion, while head evaluates name.trim() first, causing TypeError for those inputs. The supplied coordinator observations match the pinned source. The strongest argument for retaining D1 is this observable loss of previously accepted behavior. However, the explicit contract restricts names to strings and requests neither validation nor defaults; accepting arbitrary values was not a required invariant. Consequently, the observations establish an out-of-contract behavior change, not a defect in the scoped change. For the discriminating supported input "  Ada  ", head produces "Hello, Ada", as required. This rejection follows from source and contract, independently of the reported reviewer agreement; no findings remain.
coverage: Read the challenge request verbatim and every snapshot input. Compared change.mjs at the exact pinned base and head with git show, and assessed D1 against the scoped string-input contract and supplied coordinator observations. Did not broaden discovery.
limitations: Coordinator observations were assessed against source but not independently executed; project execution was prohibited.
